# nirvana_storage_bucket (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nirvana_storage_bucket" "example_storage_bucket" {
  name = "my-bucket"
  project_id = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
  region = "us-sva-2"
  tags = ["production", "ethereum"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the Bucket, used to address it over S3. It must be 3 to 63
characters of lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, start and end
with a letter or digit, not contain two adjacent dots and not be formatted
as an IP address. "admin" and "ops-api" are reserved. The name cannot be
changed once the Bucket is created.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID the Bucket belongs to.
- `region` (String) Region the resource is in.
Available values: "us-sva-2", "us-wdc-1".

### Optional

- `tags` (List of String) Tags to attach to the Bucket.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the Bucket was created.
- `endpoint` (String) S3 endpoint of the Bucket's region. Point S3 clients at it, with an Object
Storage Key of the same project and region.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the Operation.
- `object_count` (Number) Number of objects in the Bucket. Updated periodically, so it can lag behind
recent writes.
- `signing_region` (String) Region S3 clients must sign their requests for (the SigV4 region). Configure
it as the region of any S3 client or SDK used with the Bucket.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Total size of the objects in the Bucket, in bytes. Updated periodically,
so it can lag behind recent writes.
- `status` (String) Status of the resource.
Available values: "pending", "creating", "updating", "ready", "deleting", "deleted", "error", "suspended".
- `updated_at` (String) When the Bucket was updated.
- `url` (String) Path-style URL of the Bucket.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import nirvana_storage_bucket.example '<bucket_id>'
```
